courses.title: Copyediting
courses.description: Instruction in the editorial process of writing text that is clear, correct, concise, comprehensible, and consistent. Use of the Associated Press style manual and reference materials. Applying appropriate level of copyediting and eliminating bias.

courses.title: Reporting
courses.description: Reporting and writing the news. Emphasis on news gathering, interviewing and writing principles. Determining newsworthiness, using sources, writing news leads, and developing news stories. Pre or Corequisite(s): COM 106, COM 1106 , or COM 1107 .

courses.title: Public Relations Principles
courses.description: The nature and role of public relations in society, activities of public relations professionals, major influences that affect organizational behavior, and ethics and professional development of practitioners. Emphasis on management functions and developing effective public relations strategies.

courses.title: Public Relations Writing
courses.description: Format and style for writing public relations materials. Emphasis on writing the various types of public relations copy. Writing-Intensive courses must be passed with a C or higher to count towards the University’s 3-unit Writing Requirement.
courses.prerequisites: COM 1106 or COM 1107 , COM 2217 , COM 3313 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Public Relations Case Studies
courses.description: Examination of how PR professionals deal with the demanding and dynamic environment of corporate, government and nonprofit public relations. Examines situations and strategies and discusses factors that affect how public relations is practiced in organizations: identifying stakeholder groups, developing strategies, embracing diversity and recognizing ethical issues.
courses.prerequisites: COM 313 or COM 3313 , and junior or senior standing.

courses.title: Entertainment Public Relations
courses.description: An examination of public relations strategies and tactics applied within the entertainment industry including talent and media relations, reputation management, and promotional practices. Emphasis on techniques employed in major areas of entertainment public relations including music, film, theatre, TV, video games, tourism and book publishing. Students are expected to conduct research using primary and secondary sources to create press materials.
courses.prerequisites: COM 106, COM 1106 , or COM 1107 ; and COM 300 or COM 2217 . Pre or Corequisite(s): COM 313 or COM 3313 .

courses.title: Global Public Relations
courses.description: Explore the different criteria for developing or adapting PR strategies and campaigns in different regions and countries. Explore several models and scholarship that enable the ethical exploration of cultural aspects, demographics, and psychographics for audiences and stakeholders. Case studies of international public figures, organizations, and brands will be analyzed in order to provide learning enrichment opportunities.

courses.title: Persuasion
courses.description: Persuasion is examined as affected by messages in various communication contexts. The process is studied through differing aspects of source, channel(s), and receiver(s). Emphasis on contributions from behavioral theorists.

courses.title: Public Relations Campaigns
courses.description: Dive into the world of professional public relations and work directly with real clients to develop and implement a comprehensive PR campaign. Collaborate with local businesses and organizations, identify and analyze their PR challenges, craft targeted media strategies, and develop action plans to achieve tangible PR goals. Focus on client management, creating compelling media content, and developing a PR campaign portfolio.

courses.title: Crisis Communication
courses.description: [GE 4C] Theory and practice of crisis communication; strategies, and tactics when developing and implementing crisis communication plans through case studies and in-class activities.
courses.prerequisites: Junior or senior standing; and completion of GE Areas 1 and 2, or Areas A and B4 are recommended.

courses.title: Event Planning
courses.description: Application of public relations techniques to planning events. Participation in planning, organization, and implementation of selected event.
